title: A Day at the Oracle
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Put the eight steps of a consultation at the Oracle of Delphi in a valid order, then walk through the day and predict the outcome at three checkpoints: the goat test, the line for promanteia, and the form of the answer in Plutarch's day.

educational.topic: How a consultation at the Oracle of Delphi worked
learningObjectives: Explain the sequence of a Delphic consultation, from arrival to the written answer, by placing eight steps in a valid order within two attempts and choosing the correct outcome at at least 2 of 3 checkpoints.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Sequencing with rule-based feedback, followed by a step-through walk with predict-then-reveal checkpoints
keyQuestions: What must happen before a consultant hears Apollo's answer?
What happens if the goat does not tremble?
Who goes first when a Lydian envoy and an Attic farmer are both waiting?
In what form did the answers come in Plutarch's day?
commonMisconceptions: Anyone could walk in and ask at any time.
The fee was the only cost of a consultation.
The oracle answered everyone in the same order.
The god could always be made to answer.
The Pythia always answered in verse.
assessmentOpportunities: A valid order within two Checks.
First-attempt score on three checkpoints (mastery: 2 of 3).
Name two gates that could keep a consultant from the god's answer and who controlled each.
